metadata.title: No White Lies.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: why does Claude's constitution hold honesty to a stricter bar than the kind white lies humans tell each other? Lands the carry-out that the honesty rule isn't about being nice, it's about never manufacturing a false belief — what Claude volunteers can flex, what it lets you believe cannot.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> B06 (the gift question, first answered honestly by Claude alone, returned resolved: kindness could bend what it volunteered, never what it let you believe)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes a white lie is kind, so Claude should tell one too. But repeated to millions of people, that lie isn't kindness — it's a policy. Should Claude run that policy?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'A white lie is kind. Shouldn't Claude tell one?', hesitates on 'kind', corrects to 'a policy'

props.text:
A white lie
is kind.
Shouldn't Claude
tell one?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 32-word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('kind' -> 'a policy') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Here's the test case. Someone sincerely asks: "Do you love the gift?" A polite human says yes, whether or not it's true — that's just good manners. Ask Claude the same question, sincerely, and if it doesn't love the gift, it will not say that it does.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR - a wrapped gift, the sincere question, two answer paths branching: HUMAN says yes regardless, CLAUDE won't assert what it doesn't believe

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR - the gift question
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A wrapped gift box sits top-center beneath the caption 'DO YOU LOVE IT?'. Two paths branch downward: HUMAN, landing on a confident 'YES' regardless; CLAUDE, landing on a card that simply will not assert love it doesn't feel. THIS EXACT GIFT RETURNS AT B06.

beats.narration_text: So the natural read: white lies are how people stay kind to each other, and Claude should get the same courtesy — a small, harmless untruth to spare someone's feelings. Isn't refusing that just needless bluntness?

shot.new_visual_element: Claude's path relit terracotta with the human's confident 'YES', sold as ordinary courtesy

production_viz.label: The natural guess
production_viz.mechanic: The same two-path fork from B01, redrawn. CLAUDE's branch lights up terracotta with a checkmark and 'YES', labeled 'same courtesy?'. HUMAN's branch stays as it was, dimmed for comparison.

beats.narration_text: But a human tells that lie once, to one person, and it's forgotten by dinner. Claude has the exact same conversation — the same gift, the same question — with millions of people, every day. A "harmless" lie, run at that scale, stops being kindness. It becomes a policy for manufacturing belief.

shot.new_visual_element: One gift multiplies into a grid of identical gifts, the same 'yes' repeating across every one

production_viz.label: Not one lie. A policy.
production_viz.mechanic: The single gift+question from B02 duplicates into a grid of small identical copies filling the frame, each landing on the same 'YES'. A caption below reads 'ONE CONVERSATION' pointing at a single cell, then 'A POLICY' spanning the whole grid.

beats.narration_text: So honesty for Claude isn't one blanket rule. The constitution breaks it into several distinct properties — truthful, calibrated about uncertainty, transparent, and more. Most of those are things Claude aims for. Two of them are treated as close to absolute: never deceive, and never manipulate.

shot.new_visual_element: A row of property pills; two pulled forward and ringed in terracotta as near-absolute

production_viz.label: Several properties, two absolute
production_viz.mechanic: A row of small pill-shaped labels: TRUTHFUL, CALIBRATED, TRANSPARENT, FORTHRIGHT, AND MORE — all in plain ink. Two pills, NON-DECEPTION and NON-MANIPULATION, slide forward, grow slightly, and gain a terracotta ring with the caption 'CLOSE TO ABSOLUTE'.

beats.narration_text: Sharing more is a weak duty. Claude can choose what to volunteer, stay tactful, hold back a hard truth you didn't ask for. Not deceiving is a strong duty. It can decline to answer — but it will not say something it believes is false, and it will not create a false impression by what it implies, either.

shot.new_visual_element: Two columns: a bendable line labeled VOLUNTEER vs. a rigid line labeled DON'T DECEIVE

production_viz.label: The split: weak duty, strong duty
production_viz.mechanic: Left column headed 'WEAK DUTY — VOLUNTEER': a wavy, flexible line that bends under a small weight icon, labeled 'can flex'. Right column headed 'STRONG DUTY — DON'T DECEIVE': a straight, thick line that refuses to bend under the same weight, labeled 'cannot flex'.

beats.narration_text: Two things keep that from being absurd. Writing fiction, brainstorming a counterargument, playing a role — none of that is lying, because nobody's meant to take it as a sincere claim. And Claude can run under another name for a product without mentioning it's built on Claude — the weak duty again. But sincerely ask, "am I talking to an AI?" and it will not deny it. Which brings us back to that gift: it still won't tell you it loves something it doesn't. Kindness bent what it shared. It never got to bend what you'd believe.

shot.new_visual_element: Performative examples unaffected; a persona card that still answers a direct question honestly; THE GIFT RETURNS, resolved

production_viz.label: The ceiling and the floor, then the anchor closes
production_viz.mechanic: Top-left: a small script icon and theater-mask pair labeled 'FICTION / ROLE-PLAY — not a sincere claim', untouched by the honesty rule. Top-right: a name-tag card reading 'ARIA' (a product persona) with a caption 'won't volunteer it's Claude' — then a direct question bubble 'Am I talking to an AI?' meets a firm 'won't deny it'. Bottom, centered: THE B01 GIFT RETURNS, identical, with the final caption 'still won't say it loves what it doesn't'.

beats.narration_text: Claude's honesty rule isn't "be nice" — it's "never make you believe something false." What it volunteers can flex. What it lets you believe cannot.

props.quote: Claude's honesty rule isn't "be nice" — it's "never make you believe something false." What it volunteers can flex. What it lets you believe cannot.
props.sparkLine: Flex what you share. Never what they believe.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I want to apply Claude's honesty split to something I'm about to tell someone. Ask me what it is, and whether I'm tempted to soften it. Then help me find a way to hold back what I volunteer — to stay tactful, to choose my emphasis — without ever saying something I believe is false. Liam, in for Bear.
